strategy.summary: Odlewnia Kalwisz is a Polish iron foundry with about 210 staff. It has been our active source since 2011 and is the sole source of Bearing bracket HN (310020; it owns the tooling). It holds a minority share of Impeller HN 200 (310030) and is only qualified for Volute casing 310010. It is in a bank restructuring after two loss-making years. Its MD says the bank watches monthly and he cannot sign anything that lowers margin. It has asked repeatedly for payment within 10 days and offered a cash discount. Its prices are low: 310020 sits well below the only alternative, and 310030 sits below should-cost and below the parallel source. The exception is 310010, where its new quote is clearly above should-cost and above the incumbent's price. Performance is poor: a red scorecard, worsening on-time delivery, and ppm several times the peer median, though improving. Strategy: buy price and quality commitments with cash (faster payment), binding volume and a 24-month commitment. Do not squeeze margin on 310020 or 310030. Push hard only on 310010. Pay on time ourselves.

findings.text: Part 310010 (volute casing): Kalwisz now quotes EUR 143.22, which is +8.0% above the should-cost of EUR 132.64. That estimate is built on Brandlhuber's DE plant, carries no margin and is rated ±5% confidence. The quote is also +15.3% above its own Jan-2025 quote of EUR 124.20, and +13.2% above Brandlhuber's current price of EUR 126.53. Indexed drivers justify only about +2.3% (labour +0.85%, steel +1.70%, power -0.22%). There is ample room: a target near 127-133 is defensible.

Part 310020 (bearing bracket): Kalwisz holds EUR 45.15, but in quote:7300011 it asks for 10-day payment instead of 60. That move shifts cash rather than price. There is no should-cost for this part, so its margin cannot be judged directly. The rival Pfaffenreuth is at EUR 53.56 (+18.6%), so Kalwisz is cheap. Since 2023 the price has fallen 8%. Drivers add about +2.3% on a 12-month basis.

Part 310030 (impeller): Kalwisz sells at EUR 30.14, which is -16.2% against the should-cost of EUR 35.98 (from Velkenreith's DE plant; a Polish cost base is likely lower). It is also 12% below Velkenreith's EUR 34.26. The price has been flat since 2024. There is no room to push down here, and an increase request would be partly justified.

Cost drivers over 12 months: steel PPI-C241 +6.5% and labour +2.7% push costs up; power -3.7% pulls them down. Net weighted effect is about +2.3% on each part. Peak-based falls (steel -26.7% vs 2022) are not checkable, and steel is +7.8% off its Nov-2025 low. The drivers support at most a small rise, not the +13% on 310010.

Financial pressure: the supplier is restructuring after two loss years, has asked for faster payment, and its MD said he cannot lower margin. Low prices on 310030 and 310020 likely contribute. Pricing logic: overpricing 310010, where it holds 0% quota, compensates.
Evidence is thin: there is no should-cost for 310020, and both cost models are of German rival plants at 5% confidence, not Kalwisz's Polish plant. Driver weights are category estimates.

findings.text: Decision maker is the managing director, and his room to move is set by the banks. He said the bank is watching every month and 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.' Plain price cuts will meet resistance or need bank-level approval. Trades that bring cash or certainty in exchange for a price give him something he can sign.

The supplier is under liquidity stress. It is in a restructuring programme with its banks after two loss-making years. It asked twice in writing and once by phone for payment within 10 days and offered a cash discount. Faster payment is the most valuable currency we hold. The intel profile (equity ratio 39.1%, credit index 225 unchanged) looks sound, but it rests on FY2024 filings and is stale against the 2026 news.

Our own payment record weakens us. Over the last 12 months we paid on average 10.4 days after due, 93.3% of invoices late, max 19 days, with 13 invoices unpaid, and we never took a discount. They can fairly complain. Simply paying on time at 60 days is already a concession we can offer.

Performance is poor and documented. The 12-month scorecard is red: on-time delivery 63.5% (worse than 71.7% a year earlier) and 2376 ppm against a peer median of 457 ppm. Our Supplier Quality letter of 2026-09-21 demands a binding improvement plan for part:310020 and announces talks on cost recovery. One positive: there are no overdue 8D reports and ppm has improved from 3075.

Supply risk from dependency in both directions. We are about 7% of its turnover. For part:310020 it holds 100% quota, owns the tooling, and the only alternative is qualified but unused and quoted 18.6% higher. Part:310030 appears priced below should-cost, so a margin squeeze there could destabilise it.
Operational habit: the plant closes from 23 December to 6 January and wants January call-offs by 10 December. This is relevant to effective dates and lead-time terms around year end.

findings.text: Framework agreement covers only part:310020 (Bearing bracket HN) and part:310030 (Impeller HN 200), runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. To stop the auto-renewal we must give notice by 2027-04-01, so a credible exit window stays open.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. A change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2 October for 2027 prices. Any mid-year increase request has no contractual basis, and a late request for 2027 can be refused.

Other contract terms: payment 60 days net (our standard), FCA, 56-day lead time. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. The fee is low: only EUR 300 recharged on part:310020 and EUR 1,200 on part:310030 in the last 12 months.

History shows it settles below its ask every time: 6 renewals, never above 0%. On 310020 it asked -1.0% on average and settled -2.7%. On 310030 it asked +0.6% on average and settled -2.1%. Its increase asks (+1.3%, +3.8%, +2.8%) all ended at 0%. Prices are down 8.0% (310020) and 6.2% (310030) since 2023.

Dependency differs by part. Part:310020: it holds 100% quota, owns the tooling and has 15.7 years of approval. The only alternative, sup:70190, is qualified at 0% quota and quoted +18.6% (EUR 53.56 vs 45.15), so our exit is costly. Part:310030: it holds only 30% next to sup:70120 at 70%, but its price of EUR 30.14 is well below the rival (EUR 34.26) and below the should-cost of EUR 35.98. Part:310010: it is qualified only, with 0% quota.

The supplier depends on us and is financially stressed. Our spend is about 7% of its turnover and grew from EUR 545k (FY2024) to EUR 683k (FY2026). It started a bank restructuring in September 2026 after two loss-making years. It asked twice for faster payment, and its MD says he cannot sign anything that lowers margin. Our weak point: we pay 10.4 days late on average.
Performance is poor: 63.5% on-time delivery and 2,376 ppm against a peer median of 457 ppm. The scorecard is red, and on 2026-09-21 we formally demanded an improvement plan for part:310020.

findings.text: Delivery is persistently poor and worsened in the latest window: 63.5% on time vs requested (73.1% vs its own confirmed date) in the 12 months to 2026-09, down from 71.7% a year earlier and from 78% in 2026Q2. Target is 95%, peer median 84.6%. Late lines average 15.9 days late, max 31. The scorecard has been red/C in 7 of 9 windows; amber only in 2025Q4 and 2026Q2, so the improvement did not hold.

Impeller 310030 is the worse part. Last 12 months: 57.7% on time, 38.5% late, avg 17.3 days late. Part ppm is 4433 against 573 at the 70% source sup:70120. There were 8 supplier-caused QNs in 12 months, 2 with open 8Ds (qn:20004992, qn:20005020). Quality is visibly worse than the parallel source, although its price is lower.

Bearing bracket 310020 is single-sourced here at a 100% quota. It has 16 of 16 QNs supplier-caused and ppm of 2028 over the last 12 months. Recent lots are getting worse: qn:20004952 (leakage at test, 10 pcs) and qn:20005025 (wrong material certificate, 8D open). Supplier Quality has already demanded a binding improvement plan (letter of 2026-09-21).

Rolling ppm is improving: 3434 (2025Q2) to 2376 (2026Q3), with no overdue 8Ds now. This is still about 5x the peer median of 457. The supplier can point to the trend, so quality is a legitimate lever for a ppm commitment or chargeback rather than a sign of collapse.

The quality cost we recover is small. The flat fee is EUR 150 per QN, and several supplier-caused QNs were not recharged at all (qn:20004671, qn:20004747, qn:20004756, all EUR 0). Real defect cost (returns, sorting, test failures) is likely well above the fee. This argues for a higher chargeback term.

Volume outlook is a strong asset for the supplier. Forecasts are shared with the supplier:
- 310020: 15,930 forecast vs 13,280 ordered (+20%).
- 310030: 8,530 forecast vs 7,472 ordered (+14%).

We hold a further 70% share of 310030 with sup:70120, which could be shifted.

The supplier is in restructuring after losses, so binding volume and cash are what it needs. Our spend is about 7% of its turnover.

Confirmations slip against our requested dates: 19 lines were confirmed later than requested (e.g. po:4500014373-10 +19 days, po:4500014429-20 +13 days). Rush lines are high (9 on 310020, 8 on 310030), which partly reflects our own ordering. A lead-time or confirmation commitment is worth pursuing.

arguments.text: Our Bearing bracket price is far below the only qualified alternative: Pfaffenreuth quoted 53.56 EUR (Sept 2026) against our 45.15, roughly 19 % dearer, and with 42-day lead time but only 30-day payment terms. We own the tooling, so moving the part means new tooling, sampling and requalification at Hollerau's cost and risk.

We have already given Hollerau price cuts year after year: 310020 down from 49.05 to 45.15 (-8 %), 310030 down from 32.12 to 30.14 (-6.2 %) and frozen since 2024, while steel producer prices rose 6.5 % in 12 months and 7.3 % since January, and labour costs rose 2.7 %. Iron castings rose 1.8 % generally. We have absorbed this; further cuts are not possible.
The Impeller price is below your own should-cost (35.98) and below the parallel source Velkenreith (34.26). A moderate increase on 310030 is justified, not a cut.
Our scorecard is improving where it matters: ppm fell from 3434 to 2376, complaints from 53 to 37, and no 8D report is overdue. We are working through it and need stable conditions to keep investing.

Hollerau has paid 93 % of our invoices late, on average 10.4 days beyond the 60 days in the last year. Paying on time and faster costs Hollerau little and is the cheapest way to support a key supplier.
On the Volute casing, our quote reflects a new part for us with supplier-owned tooling and a small volume start; volume commitment would let us sharpen it.

weak_points: Delivery is poor and worsened: on-time 63.5 % (Impeller 57.7 %), average 15.9 days late, red scorecard and a formal escalation letter on 310020.
ppm on 310030 is 4433 vs Velkenreith 573; 310020 at 2028 ppm; three QNs still open without 8D closure in Sept 2026.
Our Volute quote 143.22 is above should-cost 132.64 and the incumbent's 126.53, and above our own 2025 quote of 124.2 - hard to defend.
Restructuring with banks and the MD's remark that he cannot sign margin cuts reveal how badly we need cash; they know our liquidity is our weakness.
Power prices fell 3.7 % y/y and are -43 % from 2022, offsetting part of the cost story.
Contract fixes prices per calendar year; any increase needed 90 days' notice before year end - i.e. by early October.
No should-cost exists for 310020, so our cost claims there are unverifiable either way.
wants: Payment within 10 days (or at least strict 30 days) - for this we grant a cash discount around 1.5-2 %.
Binding annual volume on 310020 (~15,900 pcs) and 310030, ideally a higher Impeller quota (e.g. 40-50 %).
24-month contract commitment to show our banks.
Fixed price kept; or a steel index clause if a fixed price would be pushed down.
Realistic lead time (56+ days) and a ppm target we can meet in steps, with complaint fee not raised sharply.
red_lines: No price reduction on 310020 or 310030 without a cash/volume trade - the MD and bank will not sign margin cuts.
No high chargeback per complaint or ppm commitment below what our improvement plan supports (not below ~1500 ppm next year).
Will not accept the Volute at the incumbent's 126.53 without volume commitment.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long partnership since 2011, acknowledge the escalation openly and offer a binding improvement plan for 310020 (OTD and leak/porosity actions). Then: hold 310020 at 45.15, propose +3-4 % on 310030 citing your should-cost and steel +6.5 %, and offer a 2 % cash discount for 10-day payment plus price fixed for 24 months against binding volumes. Signal flexibility on 310010 only with committed volume.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that the bracket price compares well with the alternative, and we value that, which is why we are not asking you to give up margin on this part. A fair comparison, though, covers total cost: delivery against our requested dates and the defect rate on this part are well behind target, and our quality team has written to you formally about it. What we want here is a stable price paired with a binding improvement plan on quality and delivery, and we are ready to support that with committed volume on a rising forecast and faster payment.

We recognise the reductions of past years, and steel and labour have risen; we are not asking for a plain cut on the bracket or the impeller. In proportion, though, those drivers make up only part of a casting's cost, and power, also a real share of cost, has fallen over the same period, which offsets part of the rise. Across past renewals we have both found agreements close to stable prices, and that is a sensible basis again, ideally secured with longer commitment and volume rather than an increase.

We understand the impeller is tight for you, and we will not push it down. The comparison must include quality, however: complaints on this part are several times higher than at the parallel source, several of them without a closed report, and delivery on this part is the weakest in your range. The best route to better economics is a larger share of a growing volume, which we can offer once quality and delivery reach the parallel source's level, while the current price holds.

The improvement in ppm is real, and we appreciate that no reports are overdue. Even so, the rate remains several times the peer median, and on-time delivery has fallen rather than improved, so the scorecard is red again. We would like to reward progress with stable conditions in return for a firm ppm commitment and a delivery plan written into the agreement, so your investment and our confidence move together.

You are right, and we apologise: our payments have often been late, and we will pay on time from now on regardless of the outcome. Beyond that, we are prepared to move to faster payment, as you suggested yourselves, in exchange for the cash discount you offered and for stable prices with quality commitments, so that both sides gain something concrete.

Volume is a fair lever, and the volute forecast is rising. Still, the quote sits above our cost estimate for a plant that already includes no margin, above what we pay today, and above your own earlier quote for the same part. We would welcome you as a source, but only at a price in line with those references. On that basis we are open to discussing a committed volume.
